talks.title: Automating DFIR The Counter Future
talks.summary:
### The Automation Wave in Digital Forensics and Incident Response
At 00:00, speaker "rainbow tables" opens a critical examination of the cybersecurity industry's rush toward end-to-end automation in Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) workflows. As security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR) platforms proliferate, organizations increasingly rely on automated playbooks to handle alert queues.

### Triage Automation vs. Sophisticated Adversaries
The speaker delineates the boundaries of automated response. While automation effectively triages commoditized threats—such as standard adware, known malware hashes, and common phishing campaigns—it cannot counter sophisticated, human-operated persistent threats that deliberately pivot around static playbook rules.

### The Economic Shift: Tool Retainers Over In-House Talent
The presentation addresses corporate financial incentives driving the automation trend. Enterprises frequently substitute internal incident response talent with automated tooling paired with third-party emergency retainers, disinvesting from internal institutional knowledge and long-term defensive research.

### The Risk of "Click Forensics" and Analyst Stagnation
A central theme of the talk is the degradation of career progression for junior defenders. When investigations are reduced to clicking through automated interface prompts ("click forensics"), emerging analysts fail to develop essential low-level skills in memory analysis, raw filesystem carving, and network packet reconstruction.

### Rebalancing Automation and Human Investigation
The session concludes with an appeal to challenge industry groupthink. Defenders must leverage automation for data enrichment and repetitive evidence collection while preserving human cognitive analysis, investigative intuition, and adversarial threat modeling at the core of DFIR operations.

talks.title: Evolving Security Operations to the Year 2020
talks.teaser: Evolving Security Operations to the Year 2020
talks.summary:
### Practical Blue Team Operations for the Next Decade
At 00:00, IrishMasms delivers an energetic guide to modernizing enterprise Security Operations Centers (SOCs) at the Blue Team Village. The presentation cuts through industry hype to provide pragmatic guidance for defensive practitioners and engineering leads.

### Securing Executive Buy-In and Strategic Funding
At 08:04, IrishMasms explains how SOC leaders must communicate security value to executive stakeholders. By mapping defensive capabilities to concrete risk reduction and regulatory compliance, security teams can secure the long-term operational budget required for staff and tooling.

### Asset Discovery and Sensor Placement Fundamentals
At 16:37, the speaker highlights visibility as the foundation of defense. A detection program is only as good as its asset inventory; teams must establish accurate counts of monitored hosts, virtual workloads, and network telemetry sources before attempting advanced analytics.

### Network Traffic Architecture: SPAN Ports vs. Dedicated TAPs
At 24:51, the presentation critiques widespread reliance on switch SPAN ports. IrishMasms warns that SPAN ports drop packets under high-load conditions and were never designed for permanent monitoring, advocating for dedicated hardware test access points (TAPs) and packet brokers.

### Vendor Evaluation and Operational Sustainability
Concluding between 33:21 and 40:00, IrishMasms offers practical advice on evaluating vendor pitches. He advises blue teams to prioritize interoperable, well-documented tooling over black-box AI platforms and to design sustainable analyst shift rotations that prevent operational burnout.
